name: Shay Boloor
zh_summary: 人們對$RKLB將Neutron延遲至2027年反應過度。$SPCX的Falcon 9大約延遲3年，Falcon Heavy近5年，但兩者都成為巨大成功。Neutron估計約26個月延遲低於行業平均約40個月。寧願看到Rocket Lab修復製造問題而非趕第一發射。Iridium的經常性衛星收入和成長中的太空系統業務提供多個增長引擎，同時建立SpaceX的可信可重複使用發射替代方案。
text:
I think people are getting too caught up in $RKLB delaying Neutron into 2027 when $SPCX Falcon 9 was roughly 3 years late and Falcon Heavy nearly 5 yet both went on to become massive successes.

This chart puts things into perspective with Neutron's estimated ~26-month delay below the ~40-month industry average and I'd much rather see Rocket Lab fix its manufacturing issues than rush its first launch.

And Iridium's recurring satellite revenue and Rocket Lab's growing space systems business give them multiple growth engines as it builds a credible reusable launch alternative to SpaceX.

ticker_notes.AMD: Trades at ~47x forward earnings with exp

zh_summary: 這是Peter Lynch最喜歡的指標，將估值與增長掛鉤，偏好使用2026至2028年窗口，以便倍數根據業務實際複合成長速度調整。例如$AMD以約47倍遠期盈利交易，但盈利預計從2026年的5.71美元增長至2028年的20.29美元，意味著約89%的盈利CAGR和約0.5倍的PEG。
text:
This is Peter Lynch’s favorite metric and I like it too because it ties valuation to growth and I prefer using a 2026 to 2028 window so the multiple adjusts for how fast the business is actually compounding.

For example $AMD trades at ~47x forward earnings but earnings are expected to grow from $5.71 in 2026 to $20.29 in 2028 implying a ~89% earnings CAGR and PEG of ~0.5x.

name: Shay Boloor
zh_summary: 相當瘋狂，GPU現在是AI供應鏈中唯一平衡的部分，而DRAM、SSD、硬碟和晶片基板面臨比正常長2-5倍的交貨時間。這意味著即使$AMZN、$MSFT、$GOOGL和$META確保了他們的$NVDA GPU，他們仍然需要CPU、記憶體和像ABF這樣的封裝材料，這些可能需要近一年才能採購，而正常只需三個月。這對$MU和$SKHY在DRAM和HBM、$SNDK在企業SSD、$WDC和$STX在硬碟以及$INTC和$AMD在CPU方面是巨大機會，因為AI代理推動整個基礎設施堆疊的需求。
text:
Pretty wild that GPUs are now the only balanced part of the AI supply chain while DRAM, SSDs, hard drives and chip substrates face lead times 2–5x longer than normal.

That means even if $AMZN, $MSFT, $GOOGL and $META secure their $NVDA GPUs, they still need CPUs, memory and packaging materials like ABF that can take nearly a year to source versus just three months normally.

That's a massive opportunity for $MU and $SKHY in DRAM and HBM, $SNDK in enterprise SSDs, $WDC and $STX in hard drives and $INTC and $AMD in CPUs as AI agents drive demand across entire infrastructure stack.

- Government will never stop printing money, so bitcoin / gold / land will all do well for 2 decades

- AI is drastically underestimated and the best AI companies are significantly undervalued

- Shorting individual stocks is very difficult, so I wouldn’t try it but the biggest indicator of whether a company survives or not is the internal speed of iteration now 

- Bonds shouldn’t be in the conversation for anyone under age 50. Picking up pennies in front of steamroller 

- Venture investing & public markets will blend in next 5 years, so private valuations will rise due to lots more capital chasing a few great companies

- Young people should look at assets & markets that Wall Street hasn’t adopted yet. This used to be bitcoin/crypto, but now private markets, prediction markets, compute markets, and data brokering

- every investor should be sovereign. You can use a financial advisor, but you have to know your numbers, your strategy, and your risk exposure. AI makes this too easy (Silvia .com)

- Everyone arguing over interest rates, oil, and other historical macro factors are not wrong, but these just have less impact today (thx @jvisserlabs)

- agents are coming for finance and things are going to rapidly change. Don’t fight it, embrace it and use to your advantage.

- Tesla / SpaceX merger will happen and create largest company in human history. My simple rule is to never bet against Elon.

There are many more, but what are yours?

And getting that power into AI data centers creates another opportunity for $VRT in power delivery and cooling, $FPS in transformers and prefabricated electrical systems and $ON and $NVTS in improving efficiency through SiC and GaN.

name: Serenity

ticker_notes.SIVE: 已籌7億瑞典克朗，無融資壓力

zh_summary: @aleabitoreddit：$SIVE瞄準一級超大規模雲端業者的可插拔、CPO及NPO部署，透過Ayar、$JBL、$GFS及O-Net進行上游認證，最終可能流向$AMZN或$MSFT；$CIFR等託管業者仍需10億美元以上融資，$CRWV等新雲端需數十億美元，利率上升令其更困難，而$SIVE已籌集7億瑞典克朗並依賴外部晶圓廠；他認為即使超大規模業者AI資本開支下降，光學領域仍不受影響。
text:
Few things:

- $SIVE is targeting T1 hyperscaler deployments for pluggables, CPO, NPO. Not quite sure what you mean by Tier 2. 

They have direct engagements with hyperscalers but currently are more upstream by qualifying with companies like Ayar, $JBL, $GFS, O-Net that eventually likely ends up -> $AMZN / $MSFT for example. 

On financing: 

- Colo players like $CIFR still need $1B+ of financing for their sites.
- Neoclouds like $CRWV need billions of financing to buy GPUs.

Higher rates + less support for financing makes it more challenging for these players. 

$SIVE already raised 700M SEK for their buildout and largely rely on external foundries, so they don't have financing constraints. 

There's pressure on players that need currently need financing for capex, but markets group up everyone in AI sector indiscriminately. 

The second nuance is whether or not this effects the end customers in terms of demand. 

I'd argue optical sector is insulated, even if overall AI capex from hyperscalers decreases, I see optical content still rising and aggregate demand rising. 

And this is especially the case with new incoming players going through their first qual cycles.

- Q2 2026: 50-60% increase
